title: Conditions
description: Teach your programs to make decisions with if, else and elif.

subLevels.title: Comparisons
subLevels.summary: Compare values and get True or False.

blocks.text: Comparison operators compare two values. The answer is always True or False.

explanation: 4 is not equal to 5, so False.

blocks.text: == compares. A single = stores a value.

questions.explanation: >= is True when the left side is greater than OR equal to the right.

questions.prompt: Which operator checks if two values are equal?
questions.explanation: == compares values; = assigns a value to a variable.
10 is not less than 3, so the comparison is False.

subLevels.title: if and else
subLevels.summary: Run code only when a condition is True.

explanation: So the indented line underneath runs.
Notice the colon : at the end of the if line.

blocks.text: Python uses indentation (4 spaces) to know which lines belong to the if.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Forgetting the colon or the indentation is the most common beginner error.

explanation: 15 > 25 is False, so the if block is skipped.

questions.prompt: What must end an if line?
questions.explanation: Every if, else and elif line ends with a colon.
3 > 10 is False, so the else branch runs.

questions.prompt: How does Python know which lines belong to an if?
questions.explanation: Python groups code by indentation, usually 4 spaces.

blocks.text: elif (short for else if) lets you test another condition when the first one is False.

explanation: 72 >= 90 is False, so Python moves on.
72 >= 60 is True — Grade B is printed.
Once a branch runs, the rest are skipped.

blocks.text: Python checks conditions from top to bottom and runs only the first one that is True.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Put the most specific condition first.

questions.explanation: elif is short for else if.
50 > 80 is False; 50 > 30 is True, so Medium prints and the rest are skipped.

questions.prompt: How many branches of an if/elif/else chain can run?
questions.explanation: Only the first branch whose condition is True runs (or else if none are).

projects.title: Movie Ticket Pricer
projects.summary: Work out a cinema ticket price from age and day using if, elif and else.

briefing.title: Build a Movie Ticket Pricer
text: A cinema charges different prices for children, students, adults and seniors, with Rs 50 off on Tuesdays. Your program works out the price.
Pick the right line at each stage and watch the program grow.
why: Shops, buses and apps all use rules like these to set prices
It practises comparisons and choosing between several options with elif
briefing.sampleOutput:
=== Movie Tickets ===
Your age: 15
Day (e.g. Tue): Tue
Ticket price: Rs 70
Enjoy the movie!

stages.title: Ask for the age
stages.instruction: Print a title, then ask for the user's age. We'll compare it with numbers, so it must be a number.

question.prompt: Which line reads the age as a number?
question.explanation: int() turns the typed text into a whole number, so age < 5 works (1.4).

optionFeedback: age would be text, and comparing text with 5 is a TypeError.

stages.title: Ask for the day
stages.instruction: Ask which day it is. Days are words like Tue, so keep the answer as text.

question.explanation: Words stay as text, so plain input() is right (1.4).

optionFeedback: int() can't turn Tue into a number. This is a ValueError.

Words stay as text, so plain input() is right (1.4).

stages.instruction: Children under 5 go free. Start the price rules with this check.

question.prompt: Which line starts the check for small children?
question.explanation: if, a comparison, then a colon. The indented line below runs only when it's True (2.2).

stages.title: More age groups
stages.instruction: Under 18 pays Rs 120 and 60 or over pays Rs 100. These checks should only happen if the earlier ones were False.

question.prompt: Which line checks the next age group?
question.explanation: elif is checked only when everything above it was False, so a 3-year-old stays free (2.3).

stages.title: Everyone else
stages.instruction: Anyone who didn't match a rule above is an adult and pays Rs 200.

question.explanation: else needs no condition: it runs when every check above was False (2.2).

stages.title: Tuesday discount
stages.instruction: On Tuesdays every ticket is Rs 50 cheaper, but a price can never go below 0.

question.prompt: Which line gives the Tuesday discount?
question.explanation: Work out price - 50 and store it back in price (1.2). The next check stops it going below 0.

optionFeedback: Work out price - 50 and store it back in price (1.2). The next check stops it going below 0.
This works out the answer but throws it away. The price doesn't change.
This sets every Tuesday ticket to Rs 50 instead of taking 50 off.
== only compares. The price doesn't change.

stages.title: Show the price
stages.instruction: Print the price, then a special message when the ticket is free.

question.prompt: Which line checks for a free ticket?
question.explanation: == checks whether two values are equal (2.1).

optionFeedback: = stores; it can't be used in a condition. This is a SyntaxError.
price is the number 0, not the text "0", so this is never True.

walkthrough: int() turns the age into a number; the day stays as text.
if / elif / elif / else picks exactly one price. Order matters: the first True check wins.
On Tuesday, 50 is taken off. If that makes the price negative, it is set back to 0.
A 15-year-old pays 120, minus 50 on Tuesday: Rs 70.
